executive_summary: Coverage/wire fix of an instrument that already exists and is wired — the migration apply-state verifier and its CI drift gate. Premise VERIFIED TRUE at LEAD (a first this session): the verifier scans only database/migrations (verify-migration-apply-state.mjs:30), the gate's push filter never re-triggers on database/functions/ / database/manual-updates/ / supabase/migrations/, and the gate's final wiring-proof step runs a db-project vitest test that CI's disabled db project turns into 'No test files found' exit 1 — red on every run regardless of drift verdict (empirically corroborated: GH run 31359162717). VALIDATION measured three load-bearing corrections now folded into the FRs: (1) disposition-ledger keys are BASENAMES end-to-end by documented design, and 5 basenames exist in BOTH database/migrations and supabase/migrations (one with DIVERGENT content) — naive multi-root scanning would let one disposition suppress two different files and make the ledger-sync step an order-dependent flake; (2) the LEAD-FINAL chairman-apply-state gate matches migration declarations by exact string — the new-root repo-relative id IS the declaration contract; (3) the wiring-proof test needs no db-project gating at all (it imports no db setup) — RELOCATING it so the proof actually RUNS in CI beats warning-and-skipping, which would recreate 'green forever, asserting nothing'. Also measured: extending the scan surfaces exactly ONE genuinely new blocking gap (supabase/migrations/20260625_eva_stage_gate_results_outcome.sql, live-verified NOT_APPLIED) — the gate is ALREADY red with 10 pre-existing recent gaps, so 'gate is green' is explicitly NOT an acceptance criterion; the gaps are the gate working.

functional_requirements.title: Multi-root scan with collision exclusion — every migration location visible, no basename ever suppresses two files
functional_requirements.description: Extend scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs to scan database/functions/, database/manual-updates/, and supabase/migrations/ (*.sql only; ARTIFACT_RE exclusion tested on the basename) alongside the primary root. Primary-root files keep BARE BASENAME ids (the disposition ledger's documented basename keys stay byte-stable); new-root files get REPO-RELATIVE ids ('supabase/migrations/x.sql'). Content resolution: id contains '/' → resolve from repo root, else from MIGRATIONS_DIR. migrationDateToken/isRecent/orderMigrations extract from path.basename(id) (back-compat: basename of a basename is itself) so a recent-dated new-root file classifies RECENT — without this the prefixed id silently classifies LEGACY, a fail-open. COLLISION EXCLUSION (the VALIDATION-critical correction): a new-root file whose basename already exists in the primary root is EXCLUDED from the scan and reported loudly to stderr with a content-comparison verdict (byte-identical → benign copy note; DIVERGENT → named explicitly — the live specimen is 20251129_musk_algorithm_pareto.sql). Exclusion, not dual-keying: ledger keys, suppressedBasenames() and gapBasename() all strip to basename by documented design, so admitting a colliding id would let one disposition suppress two different files and make buildLedger() order-dependent. ENOENT on a configured new root warns to stderr and continues (files gone from git = nothing to verify); any other readdir error stays fail-closed MISCONFIG, matching the existing unreadable-entry posture.
acceptance_criteria: POSITIVE: with the real repo, --json output contains database/functions/semantic_code_search.sql and repo-relative ids from database/manual-updates/ and supabase/migrations/ — the exact file that slipped merged-not-applied this week is visible to the audit.

NEGATIVE (key stability): every database/migrations id in the output is a bare basename, byte-identical to the pre-change format — the committed disposition ledger and its seeder diff stay stable (the gate's ledger-sync step must remain green on merge).

COLLISION: a new-root file with a primary-root basename twin is excluded and loudly reported with the content verdict; proven two-sided with fixture roots (identical twin → note; divergent twin → named).
RECENT classification: a new-root file dated >= cutoff classifies RECENT (basename extraction proven — a prefixed id must not silently classify LEGACY).
Non-.sql files in the new roots (the 9 .md files in manual-updates) never enter the scan.
ENOENT on a configured root → stderr warning + scan continues; a non-ENOENT readdir error → MISCONFIG (fail-closed), both pinned.

functional_requirements.title: Gate re-triggers on every migration location
functional_requirements.description: Add database/functions/*.sql, database/manual-updates/*.sql, and supabase/migrations/*.sql to the workflow's push path filter so a merge touching only those dirs re-runs the drift gate. The daily cron remains the backstop for anything else.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow push paths contain all three new globs (pinned by a static unit test on the workflow YAML, precedent-style).
Existing filter entries are untouched (verifier, guards, workflow, ledger, ledger-reader).

functional_requirements.title: Harness/verdict separation — the wiring proof RUNS in CI, and harness unavailability can neither mask nor impersonate a verdict
functional_requirements.description: TWO layers, per the VALIDATION reframe. LAYER 1 (the real fix): tests/integration/migration-apply-state-ledger-wiring.test.js is routed to the gated db project purely BY DIRECTORY — it imports only vitest/child_process/fs/path/url, never touches setup.db.js, and needs credentials only for the verifier subprocess the workflow step already supplies. Relocate it so it actually executes in CI (move to tests/unit/ or include via a dedicated vitest project pattern mirroring the SMOKE_INCLUDE precedent at vitest.config.js:147). Do NOT set VITEST_DB_ALLOW_REF — that authorizes all 225 db suites against production secrets. Budget for first-run failure: the suite hardcodes a fixture filename (20260713_quick_fixes_factory_lane.sql) and has likely never executed in CI — fix what it finds, don't skip it. LAYER 2 (defense in depth): the workflow step separates outcomes — proof ran and passed → OK; proof ran and failed → gate FAILS (real verdict); harness could not run the proof ('No test files found' signature) → loud ::warning explicitly stating the proof did NOT run, exit 0 — never a red that impersonates a drift verdict, never a silent green that claims the proof ran. EXPLICITLY NOT AN AC: 'the gate is green'. The strict verifier step reds today on 10 pre-existing genuine recent gaps (12/12 recent runs) and will surface one more (the eva_stage_gate_results gap) when FR-A lands — the gaps are the gate WORKING; applying them is chairman-gated and out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: The wiring-proof test executes in CI's unit-tier vitest invocation (proven by it appearing in the run's collected tests, not by absence of error).
Two-sided step logic (pinned by a static workflow test): a genuine test failure exits 1; the no-test-files signature warns loudly (message states the proof did not run) and exits 0.
The relocated test passes locally against the real verifier; any hardcoded-fixture breakage found is fixed, not skipped.
No VITEST_DB_ALLOW_REF anywhere in the workflow.

functional_requirements.title: Dispositions and declarations for the newly-visible corpus
functional_requirements.description: Run the disposition seeder over the extended gap set and commit the ledger delta (reason-required per the ledger contract; buildLedger writes only auto-classifiable entries — measured: 3 entries from 130 gaps today, so expect a small delta). Record the expected merge-day observable in the PR: exactly ONE new RECENT red line (supabase/migrations/20260625_eva_stage_gate_results_outcome.sql, live-verified NOT_APPLIED — its byte-identical 20260731 sibling classifies APPLIED). Document the declaration contract for the LEAD-FINAL chairman-apply-state gate at the choke point: declarations for new-root migrations must name the REPO-RELATIVE id (the gate matches by exact string; the colliding-basename hazard is closed by FR-A's exclusion). Route the divergent-content twin specimen (20251129_musk_algorithm_pareto.sql) to the durable feedback channel.
acceptance_criteria: The gate's ledger-sync step verdict is unchanged by this SD (seeder re-run produces the committed ledger).
The one-new-red-line expectation is stated in the PR body (so merge-day observers read it as the gate working, not breaking).
The declaration-contract note exists at the verifier or gate choke point (repo-relative ids for new-root declarations).
The divergent twin is recorded in the feedback channel with both paths.
